## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best tide.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best swell direction.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the wave size this break works in.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Read directly: Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, WSL x2, Surf Atlas, National Surfing Reserves, Experience Gold Coast, City of Gold Coast, Wikipedia (Burleigh Heads suburb page, which has only a short surfing note). Could not read: SurferToday (403), mondo.surf and surfnerd (403, found by search). WIND: Surf-Forecast's SW offshore matches the profile. Surf Atlas's winter southerly offshores sit at the 45 deg boundary. WSL says northerlies are the dreaded wind. WannaSurf's NW/W is the outlier. SWELL DIRECTION: SSE (Surf-Forecast), SE (WannaSurf), SE-S (Surf Atlas); readable sources lean slightly south of the profile optimum max of 150, so consider ~100-165. TIDE is in conflict: Surf-Forecast and WannaSurf say all tides (WannaSurf prefers rising). Experience Gold Coast says a rising mid tide is safer but the lower tide gives racetrack sections, which supports low_to_mid; SurferToday's 'lower tides' is unreadable. Surfing Reserves notes the Cove's rocks are exposed at low tide. SIZE: WannaSurf starts at 5-6 ft and holds 10 ft+, and WSL says it handles sizable swell better than nearby spots. The profile's 3-12 ft is broadly consistent, though WannaSurf's minimum is 5 ft. PERIOD: no seconds; Surf-Forecast says a mix of groundswell and windswell. SEASON: Surf-Forecast and Surf Atlas both say winter (Jun-Aug), which conflicts with the profile's Jan-Jun emphasis. Only SurferToday (unreadable) gives Dec-Mar, and WSL notes the January event often meets summer flat spells. BATHYMETRY: a sand-over-rock point (WannaSurf, Surfing Reserves, WSL 'sandbar'). Tallebudgera Creek feeds shifting banks (Surf Atlas). WannaSurf dates beach bulldozing to 1999-2000. No measured survey or peer-reviewed study was found (Crossref searches returned nothing relevant).

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 5–6 ft | documented | S3 | `wave_height_min_ft` 3 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | — | not documented | — | no separate setting; working range 3–12 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 10 ft | documented | S3, S4 | `wave_height_max_ft` 12 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at 1.5-2 m / 5-6 ft (the page's own conversion; it does not say face or offshore height).
  - S3 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.5m-2m /5ft-6ft and holds up to 3m+ / 10ft+”
- **Ideal range**: No excerpt states an ideal or best size range.
- **Maximum suitable**: WannaSurf says it holds up to 3 m+ / 10 ft+, an open-ended bound (scale not stated), and WSL says it takes sizable swell better than many other local spots, without a number.
  - S3 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.5m-2m /5ft-6ft and holds up to 3m+ / 10ft+”
  - S4 (World Surf League): “It too has a long righthand barrel that takes sizable swell a bit better than many other local spots.”

- **Sheltering**: Surf-Forecast says there is some shelter here from south winds; no strength is given.

  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Good surf at all stages of the tide.”
  - S3 (WannaSurf): “Best tide positionAll tides...Best tide movementRising tide”
  - S2 (SurferToday): “Burleigh Heads generally works best on lower tides.”
  - S8 (Experience Gold Coast (tourism)): “A rising mid tide is safer as rocks are present here...you'll get away with the lower tide where fast racetrack sections”
- **Rising or falling**: WannaSurf gives the best tide movement as rising, and Experience Gold Coast says a rising mid tide is safer.
  - S3 (WannaSurf): “Best tide positionAll tides...Best tide movementRising tide”
  - S8 (Experience Gold Coast (tourism)): “A rising mid tide is safer as rocks are present here...you'll get away with the lower tide where fast racetrack sections”
- **Size-dependent preference**: No excerpt ties the tide preference to swell size; National Surfing Reserves says only that the Cove's rocky bottom is exposed at low tide.
- **Local tide data**: App tide data, not research evidence: data/tide_stations.json links this spot to the EOT20 global tide model cell eot20:burleigh-heads (datum model mean sea level), 6.0 km from the break, as primary (looked in data/tide_stations.json, data/tides/constants_eot20.json and docs/tides.md); the app shows predicted astronomical tides only.

- **Prime months**: Surf-Forecast says winter is the best time of year and Surf Atlas says Burleigh fires on the SE winter swells (both encoded June-August in the evidence), while SurferToday (search summary) says the most reliable season is December to March.
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Winter is the best time of year for surfing here.”
  - S6 (Surf Atlas (thesurfatlas.com)): “The Burleigh Heads surf enjoys the same SE winter swells that the rest of the Gold Coast harvests to fire up its point breaks.”
  - S2 (SurferToday): “The most reliable season is December to March, when east wave trains and southeast and south groundswells arrive.”
- **Secondary season**: No excerpt states a secondary or shoulder season.
- **Swell sources**: SurferToday (search summary) names east wave trains and southeast and south groundswells, and Surf Atlas the same SE winter swells that feed the other Gold Coast points.
  - S2 (SurferToday): “The most reliable season is December to March, when east wave trains and southeast and south groundswells arrive.”
  - S6 (Surf Atlas (thesurfatlas.com)): “The Burleigh Heads surf enjoys the same SE winter swells that the rest of the Gold Coast harvests to fire up its point breaks.”
- **Wind patterns**: SurferToday (search summary) says winter brings a consistent southwest offshore and that northerlies are too onshore from September to December, Surf Atlas speaks of dominant winter southerly offshores, and WSL says the January event has met summery flat spells and dreaded northerlies.
  - S2 (SurferToday): “Winter can produce bigger waves with a consistent southwest offshore wind.”
  - S6 (Surf Atlas (thesurfatlas.com)): “the angle of the coast here is also perfect for the dominant winter southerly offshores”
  - S2 (SurferToday): “Northern winds are too onshore from September to December.”
  - S5 (World Surf League): “the Flight Centre Burleigh Pro has had this misfortune of coinciding with summery east coast flat spells, and dreaded northerly winds”

## Conflicting information

- **Tide · preferred stage**: Surf-Forecast and WannaSurf say all tides, SurferToday (search summary) says lower tides, and Experience Gold Coast says a rising mid tide is safer because of rocks while the lower tide gives fast racetrack sections.
- **Seasonality · prime months**: Surf-Forecast says winter is the best time of year and Surf Atlas says Burleigh fires on the SE winter swells (both encoded June-August in the evidence), while SurferToday (search summary) says the most reliable season is December to March.
